note: SCG I.18 n.4 says the composer is the efficient cause of the composite. It bears on the premise but does not state it: the premise says the uniter causes the composite's esse (CausesIn c x esse), and the passage names neither esse nor the step from efficiently causing a composite to causing its being; DISAMB-UNITING-CAUSE keeps EfficientlyCausesIn and CausesIn apart. No passage searched in SCG I-III (Corpus Thomisticum, 2026-11-05) states that the composer or uniter gives the composite its esse.
